title: Two Sheriffs and a River
subtitle: Crow's Ford and Villa del Cuervo, Thursday to Saturday: Two Claims to One Jail, a Valise of Railway Money, a Feast Day and a Rope

setting.name: Crow's Ford, Texas, and Villa del Cuervo, Tamaulipas, Thursday 14 to Saturday 16 May 1874
setting.description: The border town. Crow's Ford is an adobe and sandstone town of eight hundred on the Texas bank of the Rio Grande, forty miles above Rio Grande City, with a plaza, a church, a customs house, a stage station and two men who both say they are sheriff of the county. Matías Uresti was appointed under the old government in 1872 and holds the jail, the county records and the keys; Hollan Purcell was put in by the new county commissioners in March and holds the courthouse and a warrant. Neither will yield until a district judge rules, and the district judge comes in October. Across the river, by Zenaida Arizpe's ferry, Villa del Cuervo is older and twice the size, with its own alcalde, its own garrison, its own feast day on Friday and its own long memory of Texans with guns. Into this the party ride on Thursday, a day ahead of the Riders or a few hours, and find that the new sheriff is holding Isom Haywood's brother-in-law in a warehouse to make him talk, that a railway man is on Friday's stage with a valise of money, and that by Friday night there will be a rope on the plaza. The scenario is a small sandbox of named people with competing claims on the same few square blocks, and it ends with the party knowing where Isom is and riding for Palomas Bend, with the Riders behind them, ahead of them, or alongside.
setting.atmosphere: Heat and river light. The Rio Grande in May, low before the June rise, a quarter mile of brown water and sandbars with the ferry crossing on a rope and the Mexican bank green with cane and willows. Adobe walls the color of the riverbank, whitewashed churches, flat roofs with parapets, ristras of chiles, a well in the plaza, goats in the streets. Spanish and English in the same sentence, and nobody thinks it strange. A customs house with a Texas flag and a lounging inspector. Across the river on Friday, the feast of San Isidro Labrador: a procession of farmers and oxen with flowers on their horns, a priest blessing the fields, rockets at dusk, a band in the bandstand, dancing until midnight, the smell of roasting goat and the sound of guitars across the water. On the Texas side that night, men drinking in the cantina, and later, torches. The tone is a western at its most political: everybody has a claim, a grievance and a reason, and the gunfight, when it comes, is about who gets to be the law.

keyLocations.name: The Plaza and the Courthouse
keyLocations.description: A dusty square with a stone well, a big mesquite tree, the church of Nuestra Señora del Refugio on the east side and the county courthouse, a two-room adobe with a flagpole, on the west. Sheriff Hollan Purcell holds the courthouse with three deputies, a county commissioners' order and a letter from Sheriff Dade Ruckert of Lockett County.
features: The mesquite tree in the plaza, with a low thick branch: the tree men look at when they talk about ropes
The courthouse: Purcell's desk, a stack of new warrants on new county paper, Ruckert's letter, and no records
The church steps, where the old men sit and watch both sheriffs
The stage station on the south side, where the Laredo stage comes in on Friday afternoon
encounters: Sheriff Hollan Purcell (Crooked Sheriff, though he is more frightened than crooked) and three Deputies
The Lockett County Riders, when they arrive (see the GAP)
Josiah Fenner, off Friday's stage
secrets: Purcell is not Vandiver's man and has never met him. He has Ruckert's letter (dated 10 April): 'Haywood's wife is one of the Cantús from up your river. He will go to her. Hold any of the family you can and wire us.' Purcell cannot wire (the nearest telegraph is Fort Ringgold's military line, and the army will not carry his messages), so he has done the first part: he arrested Dámaso Cantú when Dámaso came to town with a freight wagon on Monday. He does not know which Cantú place is Isom's: there are six Cantú families up the river. Dámaso has not said.

Purcell wants the party's help. He has read the party's letter of authority (if they show it) and sees them as allies: bring Haywood in through him, he says, and he will see the reward paid, and his claim to the office will be made. He offers them deputies' commissions, which he is not sure he has the power to give. He is an ambitious, nervous, not very bright man of thirty-five who wants very much to be sheriff and does not want anyone hanged on his plaza. When the Riders come, he discovers that he cannot stop them.
Garrett Vandiver, when he arrives, takes over Purcell. By Friday evening Purcell is doing what Garrett says, and by Friday night he is drunk in his office with the door locked.

keyLocations.name: The Jail
keyLocations.description: A thick-walled sandstone jail of 1858 a block off the plaza, with four cells, a sheriff's office, an iron door and a flat roof with a parapet. Sheriff Matías Uresti holds it, with the county records, the keys and his two sons as deputies, and has done since March, sleeping on a cot in the office.
features: The iron door, barred from inside every night
The county records in a pine press: tax rolls, deed records, the brand book, the minutes of the old commissioners' court
Uresti's office: a desk, a crucifix, a Winchester, a coffee pot, a photograph of his late wife
The roof, from which a man with a rifle can cover the plaza and the river road
encounters: Sheriff Matías Uresti, 58, and his sons Bartolo and Chema (Deputy x2)
secrets: CLUE D6a (core, automatic for anyone Uresti lets read the 1873 county tax roll, or Investigation DC 10 if they take it without him): 'Haywood, Isom. 160 acres, Palomas Bend, part of the Cantú porción no. 14. Taxes pd.' Uresti knows exactly where Isom lives and has not told Purcell, and will tell the party only when he trusts them.

Uresti does not believe the poster. He knew Isom as a sergeant at Fort Ringgold, when Isom's troop and Uresti's deputies ran down horse thieves from both banks together, and he stood up for him at his wedding. He also knows Isom is home and hurt; Inés told him in April. He has done nothing, because he cannot protect Isom from the Riders and he will not betray him to them.

Uresti's claim to the office is good in law until a district judge says otherwise, and he knows it; the new commissioners' order removing him has no authority under the statute, and Quincy Treadwell, if present, can say so in a sentence (Book Learning). He has cooperated for two years with the alcalde across the river to return stolen stock in both directions, which is why the cattle raiding in this stretch of the river is less than anywhere else, and which is why the new government wants him gone.
If the party ask Uresti to arrest anyone, he will arrest anyone: Garrett Vandiver, Gattis, Purcell, the party. He has two sons and a jail. That is the limit of his power.

keyLocations.name: The Old Customs Warehouse
keyLocations.description: A long adobe warehouse by the river landing, empty since the customs house moved, with a padlocked door and one barred window. Purcell is holding Dámaso Cantú here because Uresti holds the jail.
features: The door, padlocked, with a deputy on a chair outside by day and nobody by night until the Riders come
The barred window on the river side, at head height
Inside: an iron ring in the wall, a chain, a bucket, a blanket, and Dámaso Cantú
encounters: Dámaso Cantú, 25, Inés Haywood's younger brother, chained by the ankle
A Deputy on the door by day
secrets: Dámaso has been held since Monday without a charge or a hearing, and has been beaten once, by Purcell's deputy, not by Purcell. He will tell the party nothing about Isom: 'I don't know any Haywood.' He will talk only to Uresti, to Zenaida Arizpe, to his sister, to Doña Refugio, or to someone Doña Refugio has vouched for (a letter, a word, Saturnino).
Freed and trusting the party, he will guide them to Palomas Bend by the river trail in three hours (D6b).

keyLocations.name: El Cuervo Blanco
keyLocations.description: The cantina and hotel on the river side of the plaza: a long adobe barroom with a packed-earth floor, a zinc bar, a monte table, six rooms upstairs and a back gallery over the river. Run by a widow, Doña Natividad Saldívar, who has seen every kind of Texan and charges them all the same.
features: The monte table, dealt by Doña Natividad's son, Lupe
The back gallery, with a view of the ferry, the river and the bonfires of Villa del Cuervo on Friday night
Room 4, where Jubal Thale has been since Tuesday
encounters: Jubal Thale (Bounty Hunter) and his brothers, if they are still in the race
Rifles in the barroom, when the Riders come: Bose Harrell, a hothead who wants a showdown
Josiah Fenner, who takes the best room upstairs on Friday afternoon
secrets: Jubal Thale reached Crow's Ford on Tuesday by the Laredo road, worked out from Ruckert's letter (which Purcell showed him) that Haywood's wife is a Cantú, and has spent three days failing to learn which one. If the party saved Nate in the Colorado, Jubal tells them so, and tells them that the Riders asked him in Laredo, on Sunday, whether he had seen 'a party with a preacher and a woman doctor' (or whatever describes the party): they are hunting the party (E4). If he owes them nothing, he tells them nothing, and is a rival on the river road.

Bose Harrell, a Rifle of twenty-two with a new Army revolver and a dead brother in the Rifles' history, will call out any party member who insults Garrett or the colonel, or the Black or Mexican members of the party just for being there. Use frontier.json showdowns: the stare-down, the draw. Garrett will try to stop it, and Gattis will let it happen, because a dead party member is one fewer witness. Shooting Bose in a fair fight is legal on this side of the river and makes the party Wanted: local by Purcell's warrant within the hour.
Doña Natividad knows every family up the river and will not tell any Texan which Cantú is which.

keyLocations.name: Zenaida Arizpe's Ferry
keyLocations.description: A flatboat on a hemp rope between the Crow's Ford landing and the Villa del Cuervo landing, a quarter mile, with a palm-thatched shelter on each bank. Zenaida Arizpe runs it with her nephew, Ignacio. A Texas license on one post and a Mexican license on the other, both contested.
features: The two licenses, nailed to the two landing posts
The fare board: a person, a real; a horse, two reales; a wagon, a peso; Texans with guns, whatever Zenaida says
The rope, which Zenaida can cut from either bank in ten seconds
encounters: Zenaida Arizpe (the companion) and her nephew Ignacio, 15
Customs inspectors from both governments, who check what crosses when they are awake
secrets: Zenaida knows Isom, Inés and the way to Palomas Bend, and will tell no one with a poster (D6c). Purcell has threatened to revoke her Texas license if she will not; Capitán Galván has told her that if she carries armed Texans across without his leave, he will burn her boat. She wants a ferry both banks honor, and she wants not to be anybody's informant.

If the party win her trust (by freeing Dámaso, standing up to Purcell, a word from Doña Refugio or Uresti), she will carry anyone across the river at any hour, and she knows every ford for twenty miles, including the Palomas ford.

keyLocations.name: Villa del Cuervo
keyLocations.description: The town on the Mexican bank: a plaza with a bandstand and orange trees, the parish church of San Isidro, the casa municipal where the alcalde, Don Evaristo Lozano, sits, and the cuartel of a garrison of forty soldiers under Capitán Severo Galván. Friday is the feast of San Isidro Labrador, the town's patron: a procession, the blessing of the fields, a dance.
features: The casa municipal: the alcalde's office, a portrait of the President of the Republic, a file of letters to the American consul about stolen cattle
The cuartel: a sentry, a flag, a small cannon, forty soldiers with Remington rifles
The plaza on Friday night: lanterns in the orange trees, the band, the dancing, and families from both banks who cross for the feast
encounters: Don Evaristo Lozano, alcalde, a lawyer of fifty with spectacles and a file of grievances
Capitán Severo Galván, a professional officer of forty with orders not to let armed foreigners cross
The feast's crowd, from both banks
secrets: Don Evaristo will shelter Isom Haywood and his family if they ask, and will not hand him to Texas: the extradition treaty is for murderers and the poster is, in his professional opinion, 'a piece of advertising'. He has his own stake: he wants Uresti kept as sheriff, because Uresti is the only Texas officer in a hundred miles who has ever returned a stolen Mexican horse, and the cattle of Villa del Cuervo's ranchos have been driven across the river by Texans more often than the other way this year. He will help the party if they help Uresti.

Capitán Galván's orders, after the American army's raid across the border in Coahuila last year, are to stop any armed party of foreigners from crossing. He will enforce them against the Riders, and against the party, at the Palomas ford and anywhere else. He respects anyone who asks his leave and despises anyone who does not. A party that asks him properly, with the alcalde's word, can have it, for themselves and not for anyone hunting a man on Mexican soil.

Inés Haywood crosses from the Mexican bank on Friday evening, during the feast, with the families going back and forth, to plead with Uresti for her brother. She came down the Mexican side from opposite Palomas Bend to avoid the Texas road.

synopsis: The party reach Rancho San Lázaro with the herd on Thursday morning, are paid off, and ride into Crow's Ford at noon. They find a town with two sheriffs: Matías Uresti, the old government's man, who holds the jail and the records and knew Isom Haywood well, and Hollan Purcell, the new government's man, who holds the courthouse and Isom's brother-in-law, Dámaso Cantú, chained in a warehouse without a charge. Purcell wants the party's help to take Isom; Uresti wants them to leave his county alone. Jubal Thale is in the cantina, a rival or a friend. On Friday afternoon the Laredo stage brings Josiah Fenner, the railway land agent, with a valise and a reasonable offer: $2,000 for Isom, $5,000 for the packet, cash, today, no questions. The Riders arrive on Friday afternoon or evening, depending on the GAP, and Garrett Vandiver takes Purcell over in an hour. Across the river, Villa del Cuervo celebrates San Isidro with a procession and a dance, and the alcalde and the garrison captain have their own claims. In the evening, Inés Haywood crosses on the ferry to plead for her brother, and meets the party. Late that night the Rifles take Dámaso from the warehouse to the mesquite tree on the plaza with a rope, to make him say where Isom is, and the party must decide whether to stand in the way. By Saturday morning the party know where Palomas Bend is and so, perhaps, do the Riders.
hook: Thursday 14 May, noon. Doña Refugio pays you off at San Lázaro in silver, counted onto a blanket, and gives each of you a horse from her remuda, and says goodbye with her hand on Saturnino's shoulder. Twelve miles on, the river road comes over a rise and there is the Rio Grande, a quarter mile of brown water and sandbars and green cane, and on the near bank a town of adobe and white walls with a church tower and a flagpole, and on the far bank another, bigger, with another church tower and another flag. On the near bank, in the middle of the plaza, a big mesquite tree throws a pool of shade, and under it two men with stars on their shirts are standing ten feet apart, not talking, each with a deputy behind him, while the old men on the church steps watch them the way they would watch a dog fight.

conclusions.conclusion: D. Isom Haywood is at his own homestead, Palomas Bend, twelve miles upriver
clues: D6a: the 1873 county tax roll in Uresti's jail: 'Haywood, Isom. 160 acres, Palomas Bend' (the jail)
D6b: Dámaso Cantú, once freed and trusting the party (the warehouse)
D6c: Zenaida Arizpe, once she trusts the party (the ferry)
Inés Haywood herself, if the party win her trust on Friday night (the plaza or the ferry)
Sheriff Uresti, once he trusts the party: 'He's home, and he's hurt' (the jail)

conclusions.conclusion: B. The packet is worth more to the poster-writers than the man
clues: B5: Fenner's offer: $2,000 for Isom, $5,000 for the packet, unread (El Cuervo Blanco)

Fenner, drunk or frightened (Insight DC 14, then Intimidation or Persuasion DC 15): 'The railway can't have its title questioned. Forty-one thousand dollars of land and a depot. You understand.' (El Cuervo Blanco)
Garrett Vandiver to Purcell, overheard: 'My father wants the papers first. The man after.' (the courthouse)

conclusions.conclusion: F. Lyman Gattis killed the judge, and the Rifles burned Jubilee
clues: F1: the grey with the bar shoe at the courthouse rail (the plaza)
F2: Gattis's rifle is a Henry-pattern .44 rimfire, the caliber of the ball in the judge (the plaza or the cantina: Perception DC 12 or Wiley Dunmore)
F3: Wiley Dunmore, who has seen Gattis kill (anywhere)
C4: Garrett Vandiver, confronted with Jubilee by name, cannot answer and does not deny it (anywhere; see the scene 'Garrett')

acts.title: Act 1: Two Stars
acts.description: Thursday. The party arrive, meet both sheriffs, and learn what each wants. They find out about Dámaso. They can cross to Villa del Cuervo and meet the alcalde and the captain. Jubal Thale is in the cantina. Nobody is shooting yet; everybody is counting.
objectives: Learn the shape of the town: two sheriffs, one jail, a warehouse, a ferry, a town across the river
Choose, or refuse to choose, between Purcell and Uresti
Find out who Dámaso Cantú is and why he is chained in a warehouse
Meet the alcalde and the captain, if the party cross

scenes.name: The Standoff Under the Mesquite
scenes.description: Thursday noon in the plaza. Purcell and Uresti are disputing, again, who has the right to collect a stage line's license fee, and the town is watching. Both of them see the party ride in and both of them want to know who they are. Purcell gets there first, with an offer; Uresti waits, and watches, and asks the party to come and see him at the jail when they're ready to hear the other side.
scenes.readAloud: The younger man with the star is pale and sweating, with a new hat and a new gunbelt, and he comes across the plaza toward you with his hand out before you've dismounted. 'Hollan Purcell. Sheriff of this county, duly appointed. You'll be the Lockett County party, the hunters? I had a letter.' Behind him, under the mesquite, the older man with the other star hasn't moved: a heavy, grey-moustached Tejano of sixty in a black vest, with a Winchester in the crook of his arm and his hat pushed back, looking at you with no expression at all. 'That,' says Purcell, lowering his voice, 'is Matías Uresti, who was sheriff under the Davis people, and won't give up the jail, and I'd take it kindly if you didn't speak to him. Now. I've got something you'll want to see.'

skillChecks.success: Purcell is frightened, ambitious and not a villain: he wants the arrest because it will make him sheriff, and he hasn't thought about much past that. Uresti, watching, is the one with the authority in this town, and everyone on the church steps knows it.
skillChecks.failure: Two men with stars, each sure he's the law. The party will have to find out for themselves.

skillChecks.success: Purcell shows the party Ruckert's letter and tells them about Dámaso, the six Cantú families, and the reward. He offers them deputies' commissions. Taking them makes Purcell their friend and Uresti their opponent, at least for a day.
skillChecks.failure: Purcell is cagey: he shows them the letter but not his prisoner.

skillChecks.success: Purcell, leaned on, admits that he is holding Dámaso without a charge because he does not have the jail, and that a deputy hit him on Monday. He looks ashamed.
skillChecks.failure: Purcell calls his deputies. Uresti, under the mesquite, smiles very slightly.

scenes.name: Uresti's Coffee
scenes.description: The jail, Thursday afternoon or evening. Uresti makes coffee and does not offer to look at the tax roll. He wants to know who the party are, what they believe about Isom Haywood and what they intend. If the party tell him the truth (and they should have plenty by now), he tells them his: he knew Isom at Ringgold, he stood up at his wedding, he does not believe the poster, and he will not help anyone hang him.
scenes.readAloud: The jail office is cool and dim behind walls three feet thick, and smells of coffee and gun oil and the candle under a crucifix on the wall. Uresti pours the coffee himself into tin cups and sits down behind his desk with the Winchester across it and his hands folded on top of the Winchester. 'Señores. Señoras. You've come a long way after one man,' he says, in a slow, careful English. 'Before you ask me anything, I am going to ask you one thing, and you are going to tell me the truth or drink your coffee and go. What did Isom Haywood do?'

skillChecks.success: Uresti believes the party are not what the poster made them. He shows them the tax roll (D6a) and tells them Isom is home and hurt. He asks them to help him free Dámaso without killing anyone, and to keep the Rifles off the river road.
skillChecks.failure: Uresti thanks them for their honesty and tells them nothing. Automatic success instead if the party carry Doña Refugio's word, bring Saturnino or Wiley, or show him evidence from Bascom's Ferry (the receipts, the ball, the letter).

skillChecks.success: He already knows where Isom is, and he has been carrying it alone for three weeks, and it has worn him thin.
skillChecks.failure: A careful old lawman. He will not be rushed.

scenes.name: The Alcalde's File
scenes.description: Villa del Cuervo, Thursday or Friday, if the party cross. Don Evaristo Lozano receives Texans in his office under the President's portrait with a thick file of letters to the American consul about cattle stolen by Texans, and a short temper. Capitán Galván, if the party come armed, meets them at the landing with a sergeant and six men.
scenes.readAloud: The alcalde is a small, neat man in a black coat and steel spectacles who does not stand up when you come in, and who has a file on his desk six inches thick, tied with red tape. He puts his hand on it. 'Four hundred and twelve head of cattle and ninety-one horses,' he says, in an English better than yours, 'stolen from the ranchos of this municipality since January of last year and driven into Texas. I have written to your consul about every one of them. Your consul has not replied to one.' He takes off his spectacles. 'Now. You have come across my river with guns, on the feast of my town's saint, to ask me for something. Ask.'

skillChecks.success: Don Evaristo will help: he will give Isom and his family shelter if they cross, the party leave to cross if they come in peace, and his word to Capitán Galván to stop the Riders at the river. His price: the party help keep Uresti as sheriff, or at least do not help Purcell remove him.
skillChecks.failure: He listens courteously and promises nothing. He will think better of the party if they help Uresti on Friday night.

skillChecks.success: He knows Isom and Inés and knows where they are. He is waiting to see whether the party are worth telling.
skillChecks.failure: A lawyer with a grievance, which is real.

skillChecks.success: Don Evaristo is not intimidated, but Capitán Galván, who is in the doorway, decides the party are dangerous enough to be escorted back to the ferry with courtesy and watched from now on. Reputation in Villa del Cuervo -2.
skillChecks.failure: Capitán Galván has the party disarmed at the door by his sergeant, and their guns returned at the ferry. Reputation in Villa del Cuervo -2.

encounters: Sheriff Hollan Purcell (Crooked Sheriff) and three Deputies
Sheriff Matías Uresti and his sons, Bartolo and Chema (Deputy x2)

Capitán Severo Galván (Cavalry Trooper stats, with a sergeant and six soldiers as Cavalry Troopers) at the Villa del Cuervo landing, if the party cross armed: no combat unless the party start one, which would be an international incident

acts.title: Act 2: The Railway Man
acts.description: Friday. The Laredo stage brings Josiah Fenner at two; the Riders arrive in the afternoon or the evening, depending on the GAP (GAP 0: they are already here at noon; 1: at two, with the stage; 2: at sundown; 3 or 4: Saturday morning, and the rope scene is Purcell's deputies alone). Garrett takes Purcell over. Fenner makes his offer. Across the river, the feast of San Isidro. At sundown Inés Haywood crosses on the ferry.
objectives: Hear Fenner's offer, and decide what to say to it
Learn what the Riders know and want
See what Garrett Vandiver does when someone says 'Jubilee' to his face

scenes.name: Five Thousand Dollars in a Valise
scenes.description: El Cuervo Blanco, Friday afternoon. Fenner takes the best room, orders the best whiskey and invites the party up. He is plump, cheerful, perspiring, in a linen duster, with a valise he never lets out of reach. He knows who they are, what they have done since Bascom's Ferry, and that they are close. He offers $2,000 in cash for Isom Haywood, delivered to the Riders, and $5,000 for the packet, delivered to him, unread. He is very reasonable. He does not threaten. He mentions, in passing, that the Riders will take Haywood anyway, and that the party might as well be paid.
scenes.readAloud: He has the shutters closed against the heat and a wet towel round his neck, and a bottle of the cantina's best brandy and two clean glasses on the washstand, and he gets up from the bed when you come in and shakes everybody's hand. 'Josiah Fenner. Brazos and Gulf Railway, land department. You've had a long ride. Sit, sit.' He pats the valise on the bed beside him, an ordinary black leather bag with a brass lock. 'I'll be plain, because it's too hot not to be. In here there is seven thousand dollars in national bank notes. Two of it is for the man, which is what you came for. Five of it is for some papers the man has, which you didn't come for, and which nobody needs to read.' He pours two glasses. 'That's more money than any of you will see again in your lives. And nobody,' he says, gently, 'gets hurt.'

skillChecks.success: Fenner means the money, and he means to have the Riders kill the party after he has the packet: 'nobody gets hurt' means nobody who matters. He is also afraid of Gattis, and of Vandiver, and of being the man left holding the railway's paper when it all comes out.
skillChecks.failure: A businessman. A very reasonable one.

skillChecks.success: Valentine Shreve, or anyone who reads men at a table, sees Fenner's tell: he touches the valise when he is lying. He touched it at 'nobody gets hurt'. And he will go higher: there is more money in the railway's account at Laredo, and he can draw on it.
skillChecks.failure: His face is good. Seven thousand dollars is on the table.

skillChecks.success: The party agree to Fenner's terms and he believes them. He gives them $500 'in earnest' and tells them, to make it easier, where the Riders will be on Saturday. He is now a man who can be used, and his valise is a target.
skillChecks.failure: He smiles and says he'll think it over, and tells Garrett within the hour that the party will not sell. From now on the Riders treat the party as enemies.

scenes.name: Garrett
scenes.description: Friday, whenever the party and Garrett Vandiver are face to face: at the courthouse, in the cantina, at the ferry landing. He is polite, tired and angry, and he believes Isom murdered his cousin and the judge. The scene is the party's chance to put Jubilee in front of him. He cannot answer it. He does not change sides here; but he does not forget it.
scenes.readAloud: Up close he looks younger than he did at the fire, and very tired: a sunburned fair-haired man with his father's jaw and his mother's eyes, a good coat gone white with dust, a cavalry officer's way of standing that does not quite fit him. 'I know who you are,' he says. 'I've been a day behind you since the Brazos. You're good. My father picked you out the first night.' He looks at the river. 'Isom Haywood shot my cousin Clell through the heart in the judge's hall. Clell was twenty-two. I taught him to ride. Whatever else you've heard, that's true. You tell me where Haywood is, and you can ride home with the money, and that's the end of it.'

skillChecks.success: The party tell him what they know: the window, the rifle ball, the bar shoe, the deed book, Fenner's telegram, Gattis. He listens to all of it. Then he says 'Jubilee' himself, very quietly, for the first time, and walks away. He has not turned, but something has broken. In lb-scenario-004, at the decisive moment, Garrett will hesitate, and his Rifles will follow his hesitation.
skillChecks.failure: He says the party have been talking to the wrong people, and that Haywood's friends would say anything. But he heard it, and he does not look at Gattis for the rest of the day.

skillChecks.success: Said to his face: 'You sat your sorrel at the edge of the light and watched it burn.' He goes white, and his hand goes to his gun, and stops. He does not draw. 'I didn't know there was anyone inside,' he says, and then he realises he has said it in front of witnesses (C4).
skillChecks.failure: His hand goes to his gun. Gattis, somewhere behind him, is already ready. Run frontier.json showdowns, and have Garrett back down at the last moment; the Rifles see him do it.

scenes.name: San Isidro
scenes.description: Friday at sundown. Across the river the feast of San Isidro is at its height: rockets, the band, lanterns in the orange trees, families crossing on Zenaida's ferry in both directions. Among them, in a black rebozo, Inés Haywood comes across to Crow's Ford to plead with Uresti for her brother. The party may see her at the ferry, at the jail or on the plaza. She knows who they are: Doña Refugio's rider reached her two days ago. She has come anyway.
scenes.readAloud: She comes up from the landing among a family of farmers going home from the feast with a sleeping child on the father's shoulder, a tall woman in a black rebozo, and when she reaches the plaza and the lantern light she lets the rebozo fall back and looks straight at you. She is perhaps thirty-three, with a strong plain face and her hair in a braid, and she is not afraid of you, or has decided not to be. 'You are the ones my aunt wrote about,' she says, in English. 'I am Inés Haywood. My brother is in that warehouse because of my husband, and my husband is in his bed with a fever because of a judge, and you have come six hundred miles to take him to a rope.' She lifts her chin. 'I have come to ask the sheriff for my brother. I will ask you for nothing. But you can walk with me, if you want to hear what kind of man you are hunting.'

skillChecks.success: She is telling the truth and she is terrified, not for herself: for Isom, who is worse than she has said, and for her children, who are with him.
skillChecks.failure: A proud woman with a hard face. She means every word.

skillChecks.success: Inés believes the party will not take Isom to the Riders. She tells them that he is at Palomas Bend, that the ball is still in him and the wound has gone bad, and that he means to ride to Rio Grande City on Monday 'to see the judge's friend', and she means to stop him and take him across the river. She asks them, if they are what her aunt says, to help her do it.
skillChecks.failure: She will not tell them where Isom is. She asks them to help free Dámaso, and if they do, she tells them on the ferry landing afterward.

skillChecks.success: From her description: a rifle ball or a piece of one still in the wound, three weeks; the fever means the wound is mortifying; without a surgeon in a few days he will die. Dr. Ursula Schaller or any Doc knows this at once, and so does the table.
skillChecks.failure: He is sick. She is afraid he will die.

encounters: Josiah Fenner: no combat; he has a pocket pistol he does not know how to use
Garrett Vandiver (Gang Leader) and Gattis (Fast Gun): a stare-down, and almost a showdown
Bose Harrell (Outlaw) in the cantina: a showdown, if someone provokes it or he does (frontier.json showdowns)

acts.title: Act 3: The Rope
acts.description: Friday night, after midnight. The Rifles, with two of Purcell's deputies and half a dozen drunks from the cantina, take Dámaso Cantú from the warehouse to the mesquite tree on the plaza with a rope, to make him say where Isom is. It is a lynching, whatever Garrett tells himself; the GM should play it as a crime and a horror, not as tension to be enjoyed. Purcell is locked in his office, drunk. Uresti, his sons and the party are the only law awake. The act ends on Saturday morning with Dámaso alive or dead, the way to Palomas Bend known, and the GAP set for lb-scenario-004.
objectives: Stop the lynching, or fail to
Do it without starting a war on the plaza, if possible
Learn the way to Palomas Bend
Leave Crow's Ford ahead of the Riders, or with them, or behind them

scenes.name: Torches on the Plaza
scenes.description: At about one in the morning, twelve men with torches bring Dámaso out of the warehouse with his hands tied and a rope already round his neck, and walk him to the mesquite tree. Garrett Vandiver is not with them; Gattis is, at the back, not holding a torch. Bose Harrell throws the rope over the branch. The crowd is the Lynch Mob; the Rifles are its spine. Uresti and his sons come out onto the jail roof with Winchesters. The party have perhaps two minutes.
scenes.readAloud: You hear it before you see it, the way you hear a fire: a crowd's voice, ugly and pleased with itself, and boots in the dust. Then the torches come round the corner of the warehouse, a dozen of them, and in the middle of them a young man with his hands tied behind him and a noose round his neck, stumbling because someone keeps jerking the rope. They bring him to the mesquite. Somebody throws the rope over the low branch on the second try, and the crowd cheers the second try. On the far side of the plaza, on the jail roof, three men with rifles stand up against the stars, and an old man's voice says, in English and then in Spanish, very clearly, 'The first man who pulls that rope, I will kill.'

skillChecks.success: A voice from the party (or a shot into the air from the church steps) breaks the crowd: the drunks from the cantina melt away, Purcell's two deputies drop their torches and go home, and only the Rifles are left round the tree, eight men facing the jail roof and the party. Gattis, at the back, has already gone. The Rifles hesitate.
skillChecks.failure: The crowd roars back. Bose Harrell hauls on the rope and Dámaso's feet leave the ground. Somebody has to reach him in the next round (Athletics DC 13 to get through the crowd, or a shot to cut the rope: an attack against AC 18 with disadvantage at night).

skillChecks.success: Someone the Rifles have reason to listen to (Ulysses Wardlow's federal star, Reverend Burris's voice from Jubilee, Quincy Treadwell saying the judge's name, or the party simply telling them, loudly, what Gattis did at the schoolhouse with the lamp) stops them. Eight men stand round a tree in the torchlight with a rope in their hands, and look at each other, and one of them, Ned Purdom, if he survived Jubilee, says, 'I'm not doing this again,' and walks away.
skillChecks.failure: They are too drunk and too many. It will have to be done another way.

skillChecks.success: While the crowd faces the jail roof, someone gets to Dámaso from behind, cuts his hands free and the rope off, and gets him into the dark of the church doorway. Zenaida Arizpe's ferry is a hundred yards away.
skillChecks.failure: Someone in the crowd sees them and shouts. A fight on the plaza in the dark.

scenes.name: Saturday Morning
scenes.description: After the night: whatever happened. If Dámaso is alive and free, he, Inés, Zenaida or Uresti tells the party the way to Palomas Bend: three hours up the river trail on the Texas side, or across the river and up the Mexican bank to the Palomas ford, which Capitán Galván's patrol watches. The Riders will know the way by mid-morning, from the Cantú who freighted with Dámaso (if Dámaso talked to anyone in their hearing), or by following Inés, or from Purcell, who has found out from a freighter. Set the GAP for lb-scenario-004: the number of half-days the party will have at Palomas Bend before the Riders come up the bend.
scenes.readAloud: Morning comes up white over the river, and the plaza is empty except for a cut rope lying in the dust under the mesquite, a burnt-out torch, and the old men, who have come back to the church steps as if nothing had happened, and are talking about it in low voices. The jail door is open. Uresti is sitting in a chair in the doorway with his Winchester across his knees, unshaven, drinking coffee. He looks up at you. 'Palomas Bend,' he says. 'Twelve miles up. He is home, and he is very sick, and they will know by noon. If you are going, go now.'

skillChecks.success: The party take the Mexican bank and the Palomas ford, or the river trail with no dust, and the Riders lose their trail. GAP +1 for lb-scenario-004.
skillChecks.failure: The party take the river road, and the Riders, watching from the courthouse roof, see their dust. GAP -1 (minimum 0) for lb-scenario-004.

skillChecks.success: Capitán Galván, asked properly (with the alcalde's word, or after the party saved Dámaso), sends a patrol to the Mexican bank at the Palomas ford with orders to stop any armed men who try to cross there. He will not cross the river himself. The Riders cannot use the Mexican bank.
skillChecks.failure: Galván will keep his own bank. What happens on the Texas side is Texas's business.

encounters: Lynch Mob (the crowd), with eight Rifles in it (Outlaws x5, Hired Guns x3) and Bose Harrell; Gattis at the back, who leaves as soon as the night goes wrong
Sheriff Uresti and his sons on the jail roof (Deputy x2), who will shoot the first man who pulls the rope and nobody before
Purcell's two deputies, who go home at the first sign of resistance

A fight on the plaza, if it comes to that: torches, a mesquite tree, the well (three-quarters cover), adobe corners (half cover), a crowd running in every direction. Any shot that misses in the crowd has a 1 in 6 chance of hitting a bystander (Reputation -2 in Crow's Ford if it does)

npcsInvolved.name: Sheriff Matías Uresti, 58
npcsInvolved.role: Sheriff of the county under the old government; holds the jail, the records and the keys
npcsInvolved.description: Heavy, grey-moustached, slow-spoken, a widower with two grown sons as deputies, in a black vest with a Winchester in the crook of his arm. Born in Crow's Ford when it was in Tamaulipas. Stood up at Isom and Inés's wedding.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Keep the peace, keep the jail until a judge rules, keep Isom alive without being able to protect him, and see the Rifles out of his county.

npcsInvolved.name: Sheriff Hollan Purcell, 35
npcsInvolved.role: Sheriff under the new county commissioners' order; holds the courthouse and Dámaso Cantú
npcsInvolved.description: Pale, sweating, new hat, new gunbelt, a former customs clerk from Galveston. Not a bad man; a weak one.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be sheriff, and to make an arrest that proves it. He does not want anyone hanged on his plaza, and he will not stop it.

npcsInvolved.name: Josiah Fenner, 41
npcsInvolved.role: Land agent, Brazos & Gulf Railway; a poster-writer
npcsInvolved.description: Plump, cheerful, perspiring, a linen duster, a wet towel round his neck, a black valise with $7,000 in national bank notes.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The packet, burned. The railway's title clean. Himself out of it with his commission and his neck.

npcsInvolved.name: Garrett Vandiver, 29
npcsInvolved.description: As before, dustier and more tired; he has been in the saddle five weeks.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To finish it, to avenge Clell, and not to have to look at what he saw at Jubilee. He is beginning to fail at the last.

npcsInvolved.name: Lyman Gattis, about 40
npcsInvolved.role: The Riders' tracker; the judge's killer
npcsInvolved.description: As before. In Crow's Ford he is seen everywhere and talks to no one.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Find where Isom is. Leave no witnesses. He is beginning to think Garrett is one.

npcsInvolved.name: Inés Cantú de Haywood, 33
npcsInvolved.description: Tall, strong-faced, a braid and a black rebozo; a schoolteacher, educated at the Ursuline convent in Brownsville; mother of Lucía, 8, and Tomás, 5. Speaks English, Spanish and her mind.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Isom alive and across the river, her children safe, her brother free. She does not care about the packet, or the judge, or the grand jury, and she says so.

npcsInvolved.name: Dámaso Cantú, 25
npcsInvolved.description: A wiry, stubborn freighter with a split lip and a broken tooth from Monday, chained by the ankle in the warehouse.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To say nothing, to get out, and to get his hands on the deputy who hit him.

npcsInvolved.name: Don Evaristo Lozano, 50
npcsInvolved.description: Small, neat, black coat, steel spectacles, a lawyer trained in Monterrey; a file of stolen-cattle letters six inches thick.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Justice for his municipality's ranchers, Uresti kept in office, Isom sheltered if he asks, and no Texan with a gun telling him what to do.

npcsInvolved.name: Capitán Severo Galván, 40
npcsInvolved.role: Commander of the garrison at Villa del Cuervo
npcsInvolved.description: Lean, correct, a professional officer of the Republic with a cavalry moustache and orders from Ciudad Victoria not to let armed foreigners cross.
npcsInvolved.motivation: His orders, his country's sovereignty, and the respect of anyone who asks his leave.

npcsInvolved.name: Jubal Thale, 45
npcsInvolved.description: As before, three days into failing to find which Cantú is which.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The bounty, or, if the party saved his brother, the debt paid.

rewards.money: Fenner's $500 'in earnest', if the party took it (he will want it back, one way or another). Dámaso's thanks are not money. Uresti can pay a deputy's fee of $2 a day to anyone he swears in to keep the peace on Friday night, from his own pocket. If the party searched Bose Harrell or a fallen Rifle, about $20 each and a Stock Association letter of authority like their own.
items: The way to Palomas Bend (CLUE D6)
Ruckert's letter to Purcell, if the party took it: proof that the Lockett County sheriff told a Texas sheriff to hold an uncharged man as bait
Fenner's offer, and perhaps his $500 and his name on a receipt
Capitán Galván's patrol at the Palomas ford, if he was asked properly
Award the 7,500 XP on Saturday morning. A party at 5th level reaches 6th (14,000), and should reach Palomas Bend at the campaign's top level.

twists: Purcell is not Vandiver's man. He is a weak, ambitious man who has been handed a letter and a chance, and he is a better ally than he looks if the party give him a way to be sheriff without being a murderer: he will sign a statement about Ruckert's letter, and testify to it, for Uresti's promise to step aside in October.
Uresti has known where Isom is all along. He has been carrying it alone, and he will be relieved to share it with anyone who can help.
Inés does not want the packet delivered. She wants her husband across the river. She and the judge's last wish are on opposite sides, and the party will have to choose between them at Palomas Bend.

Fenner is the weakest of the poster-writers after Spratt. If the party get him alone, frightened, and away from Gattis, he can be turned: for a promise of immunity (which Quincy Treadwell or Ulysses Wardlow can say Ruthven might give), he will testify that the railway paid Vandiver for the depot site before the tax sales.
Gattis leaves the lynching as soon as it goes wrong. He is not interested in ropes. He has gone to find the way to Palomas Bend himself, and he may find it before the party.
dmTips: This is a sandbox of named people in a few square blocks. Write a schedule for Friday (Fenner at two, the Riders at the GAP's hour, Inés at sundown, the rope at one) and let the party move through it. Every scene they spend in one place is a scene they are not somewhere else.
Play both sheriffs straight. Uresti is right in law and Purcell is right in the eyes of the new government, and the town knows the difference between law and power better than either of them.

Villa del Cuervo is not a refuge out of a story; it is a town with its own government, interests and pride, celebrating its saint. Let the party see the feast: the oxen with flowers on their horns, the priest, the band, the dancing. Let Lozano and Galván be as formidable in their way as Uresti.

The lynching must be played as what it is: a crime, a horror, and a crowd enjoying itself. Do not make it exciting. Make it ugly, fast and stoppable. The party should feel the weight of stopping it, and the cost of not.

A showdown with Bose Harrell in the cantina is the genre's set piece and should be offered if any player wants it. Use frontier.json showdowns in full: the stare-down, the draw. Make sure the players know the legal consequences before anyone draws.

Fenner's offer is the campaign's second temptation after the poster. Put the valise on the table, open it, and let the players look at the money. Seven thousand dollars in 1874 is a fortune. If a player takes it, do not punish them for it here: the consequences come at Palomas Bend.
Set the GAP at the end of the scenario and say it aloud. It decides how much time the party have with Isom before the end.
